snp1.7:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
snp1.7:1.3: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
snp1.7:1.4: Then at that time in the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja’s residence the (sacrificial) fire was burning, and the offering had been taken up.
snp1.7:1.5: Then, as the Fortunate One was going from house to house for alms in Sāvatthī, he approached the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja’s residence.
snp1.7:2.1: The brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja saw the Fortunate One coming from afar,
snp1.7:2.2: and having seen him, he said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.7:3.1: After this was said, the Fortunate One said this to the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja:
snp1.7:3.2: “But do you know, brahmin, what an outcaste is, or what things make one an outcaste?”
snp1.7:3.3: “I certainly do not know, reverend Gotama, what an outcaste is, or what things make one an outcaste.
snp1.7:3.4: It would be good for me if the reverend Gotama would preach the Dhamma so that I may know what an outcaste is, and what things make one an outcaste.”
snp1.7:3.5: “Then listen, brahmin, apply your mind well, and I will speak.”
snp1.7:3.6: “Yes, reverend,” the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja replied to the Fortunate One,
snp1.7:3.7: and the Fortunate One said this:
snp1.7:4.1: “That man who is angry, who has enmity,
snp1.7:4.3: who has wrong views, and is deceitful,
snp1.7:4.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:5.1: Whether once born, or twice born,
snp1.7:5.2: he who is violent to creatures here,
snp1.7:5.3: who has no sympathy with creatures,
snp1.7:5.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:6.3: who is well known as an oppressor,
snp1.7:6.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:7.1: ° (He who), whether in the village or the wilderness,
snp1.7:7.2: takes by theft what is not given,
snp1.7:7.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:8.1: He who has taken on a debt,
snp1.7:8.2: and when pressed (to pay it) runs away,
snp1.7:8.3: saying: “There is no debt due to you,”
snp1.7:8.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:9.3: along the path, takes that trifle,
snp1.7:9.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:10.1: That man who, for his own sake,
snp1.7:10.2: for the sake of others, or for wealth,
snp1.7:10.3: when asked to bear witness, speaks falsely,
snp1.7:10.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:11.2: with the wives of friends or relatives,
snp1.7:11.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:12.1: He who, when his mother or father has grown old,
snp1.7:12.3: though having much, does not support them,
snp1.7:12.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:13.1: ° He who strikes, or annoys with words,
snp1.7:13.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:14.1: He who, when he is asked what is good,
snp1.7:14.2: teaches that which is not good,
snp1.7:14.3: who conceals things when he gives advice,
snp1.7:14.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:15.1: He who, having done a bad deed,
snp1.7:15.2: longs thus: “May they not know about me,”
snp1.7:15.3: he who conceals what he is doing,
snp1.7:15.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:16.1: He who, having gone to another’s family,
snp1.7:16.3: does not return the honour when (his benefactor) comes,
snp1.7:16.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:17.1: ° He who deceives a brahmin, or an ascetic,
snp1.7:17.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:18.1: ° He who annoys with words a brahmin, or an ascetic,
snp1.7:18.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:19.1: He who speaks to those who are bad here,
snp1.7:19.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:20.3: who is debased through his own conceit,
snp1.7:20.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:21.2: who has bad longings, is selfish, crafty,
snp1.7:21.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:22.2: or else one of his disciples,
snp1.7:22.4: he one should know as an outcaste.
snp1.7:23.1: He who, not being a Worthy One
snp1.7:23.2: claims that he is a Worthy One,
snp1.7:23.3: is a thief in the world with its brahmās,
snp1.7:23.4: he is the worst of the outcastes.
snp1.7:23.5: These, indeed, are said to be outcastes,
snp1.7:23.6: those whom I have explained to you.
snp1.7:24.1: One is not an outcaste by birth,
snp1.7:24.2: by birth one is not a brahmin,
snp1.7:24.3: by deeds one becomes an outcaste,
snp1.7:24.4: one becomes a brahmin by deeds.
snp1.7:25.1: You can know it also by this,
snp1.7:26.1: This Mātaṅga attained the highest repute,
snp1.7:26.2: which was very hard to obtain,
snp1.7:27.1: He ascended the way going to the gods,
snp1.7:27.3: and having put away sensual desire,
snp1.7:27.4: he went to the brahma worlds.
snp1.7:27.6: from being reborn in the brahma worlds.
snp1.7:28.1: Brahmins, though born in a family of scholars,
snp1.7:29.2: in the next life they have an unhappy destiny.
snp1.7:30.1: One is not an outcaste by birth,
snp1.7:30.2: by birth one is not a brahmin,
snp1.7:30.3: by deeds one becomes an outcaste,
snp1.7:30.4: one becomes a brahmin by deeds.”
snp1.7:31.1: After this was said, the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.7:31.3: Please bear it in mind, reverend Gotama, that I am a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life.”
